messages:
customer_acme_ops: Hey team — after we rotated the prod API key at ~08:12 UTC a subset of requests started getting 401s. Affects our image-generation and embeddings routes, about 5% of traffic. No app deploys at that time, we believe rotation went through.

sam_support: Sorry about that, we'll help dig in. Can you paste a minimal request that gets 401 (curl or fetch) and the exact response body? Also which header you send the key in?

customer_acme_ops: Thanks. Example from a failing box: 
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Api-Key abcDEF_newkey_123" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"hello"}'
```
Response: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` and body: 
```
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"The provided API key is invalid or expired."}
```
We rotated via the console and updated our secrets manager. Most hosts see success but a handful keep failing.

maya_engineer: Two quick checks: 1) Is any edge/worker or CDN doing request signing or rewriting? 2) Can you run the exact failing curl from the same host that sees 401 to confirm header and connection path?

customer_acme_ops: We do have a Cloudflare Worker that injects the key from CF KV and also some internal service workers for routing. I just ran the curl from the failing host (same IP as production) and it's the same 401.

tolga_infra: If the worker pulls the key from KV, double-check the KV binding value after rotation — sometimes the deployment uses a different binding name or an older binding value. Also CF can cache responses at the edge; a cached 401 could persist until purged.

sam_support: Can you `fetch` the worker binding directly or temporarily bypass the worker to test? Quick repro suggestion: run the curl directly to the origin but from the same host, or add a harmless custom header so we know it hit origin vs cache. Example: 
```
curl -v -H "X-Bypass-Edge: 1" -H "Authorization: Api-Key abcDEF_newkey_123" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate ...
```
If that succeeds, the edge worker or cache is the culprit.

customer_acme_ops: I tried bypass header and still 401. I then dumped network path and saw requests go through our CF worker; decided to check KV and found the deployed worker was still referencing `KV_BINDING: "prod_key_old"` — our rotation updated the secret in the console but the worker code still referenced the old binding name.

maya_engineer: That would do it — the worker was sending the old key, which is invalid post-rotation. Two follow-ups: 1) Redeploy the worker with the new binding or update the binding name to point to the new secret. 2) Purge Cloudflare edge cache just in case any 401 responses were cached.

edge-bot: cf-purge initiated by customer_acme_ops (job id cf-9932). Purge status: in progress.

customer_acme_ops: Redeployed worker to reference `prod_key_current` and forced a purge. After that ~100% success. A couple hosts that were using baked-in binaries still had old key files; rolling those fixed the remainder.

sam_support: Great — thanks for the debug steps and confirming. Summary for records: root cause was Cloudflare Worker binding referencing old KV key after rotation (and a small amount of edge-cached 401s). Remediation: update worker bindings or redeploy, purge CDN, roll affected hosts.

customer_acme_ops: Yep — marking resolved on our side. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:

maya_engineer: I'll add a short doc snippet to our rotation checklist to call out CF worker bindings + CDN purge so this is less likely to recur.

customer_acme_ops: Thanks — that would help others.

sam_support: Closing thread; ping if anything else crops up.
